title.es: El caso de la mochila perdida

es: Discutir teorías por turnos: proponer, cuestionar con una pista y acordar la más probable.

teaching.en: I think the backpack might have been taken by mistake, because there are two blue ones.
teaching.es: Creo que puede que se hayan llevado la mochila por error, porque hay dos azules.
teaching.explanationEs: Propuesta: I think + might have been + participio.
segments: I think the backpack might have been taken
by mistake, because there are two blue ones.
teaching.audioText: I think the backpack might have been taken by mistake, because there are two blue ones.

teaching.en: That is possible, but it can't have been in the canteen, because I checked there.
teaching.es: Es posible, pero no puede haber estado en la cantina, porque miré allí.
teaching.explanationEs: Objeción amable: reconoce la idea, añade but y da una razón.
segments: That is possible, but it can't have been
in the canteen, because I checked there.
teaching.audioText: That is possible, but it can't have been in the canteen, because I checked there.

teaching.en: Good point. Then chances are that it is still in a locker.
teaching.es: Buen argumento. Entonces lo más probable es que siga en una taquilla.
teaching.explanationEs: Good point acepta la objeción antes de proponer otra idea.
segments: Good point. Then chances are that
it is still in a locker.
teaching.audioText: Good point. Then chances are that it is still in a locker.

teaching.en: I agree with you: the backpack must have been left in the hall.
teaching.es: Estoy de acuerdo contigo: la mochila se debió de dejar en el vestíbulo.
teaching.explanationEs: I agree (with you): agree es un verbo, sin am.
segments: I agree with you: the backpack must
have been left in the hall.
teaching.audioText: I agree with you: the backpack must have been left in the hall.

teaching.en: I see what you mean, but the backpack may well have been taken by a student.
teaching.es: Entiendo lo que dices, pero bien puede que un estudiante se llevara la mochila.
teaching.explanationEs: I see what you mean suaviza el desacuerdo antes de but.
segments: I see what you mean, but the backpack
may well have been taken by a student.
teaching.audioText: I see what you mean, but the backpack may well have been taken by a student.

teaching.en: So we agree that it is most likely in the canteen.
teaching.es: Así que estamos de acuerdo en que lo más probable es que esté en la cantina.
teaching.explanationEs: We agree that + frase cierra el acuerdo; most likely = lo más probable.
segments: So we agree that it is
teaching.audioText: So we agree that it is most likely in the canteen.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo cuestiona Tom con amabilidad la idea de Mia?

choices.text: No, you are wrong. It was not Leo.
That is possible, but it can't have been Leo, because he was at home.
I agree, it must have been Leo.

feedback.es: Una objeción amable reconoce la idea, añade but y da una razón con because. Decir «you are wrong» es brusco y «I agree» no cuestiona nada.

hint.es: Primero se reconoce la idea; después se da una razón con but… because.

origin.text: Mia: «I think Leo took my backpack.»

prompt.es: Completa: «¡Buen argumento! Entonces se debió de quedar en la cantina.»

feedback.es: Good point es la expresión fija para aceptar un argumento antes de seguir.

origin.text: Good ___! Then it must have been left in the canteen.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Estoy de acuerdo contigo sobre la taquilla.»

answer.text: I agree with you about the locker

feedback.es: I agree with you about + tema: agree es un verbo y no lleva am.

hint.es: Empieza con el sujeto I y el verbo agree.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina Sara de la idea de Leo.

choices.text: Sara does not think Leo's idea is likely.

feedback.es: Sara dice «that is unlikely» y da una razón: los profesores estaban en una reunión.

origin.audio: Leo thinks the backpack might have been taken by a teacher, but Sara says that is unlikely, because the teachers were in a meeting.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la función que cumple en la discusión.

pairs: I think it might have been…

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene un lugar en el turno: proponer, cuestionar, aceptar y cerrar.

pairs: I think it might have been…

prompt.es: Completa: «Entiendo lo que dices, pero no puede haber sido robado.»

feedback.es: I see what you mean es la fórmula fija para reconocer la idea del otro antes de discrepar.

origin.text: I see what you ___, but it can't have been stolen.

prompt.es: ¿Quién no puede haberse llevado la bici de Tom?

feedback.es: Sara estuvo en clase todo el día, así que no pudo llevársela. Leo comió en el patio y pudo hacerlo; «Nobody» es falso.

origin.text: Case notes: Tom's bike was in the yard at lunch, and the gate was open. Sara was in class all day. Leo had lunch in the yard.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom siempre deja allí su bici, así que seguro que está en el patio.»

feedback.es: Is bound to be (o is sure to be) expresa que algo es casi seguro.

origin.text: Tom always leaves his bike there, so it is ___ to be in the yard.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué piensan las personas sobre la mochila.

choices.text: They are almost sure it was stolen.
They are almost sure it was taken by mistake.
They think it can't be in the hall.

feedback.es: «Must have been taken by mistake» expresa casi certeza de que fue un error. «Chances are» solo dice que probablemente está en el vestíbulo.

origin.audio: Mia's backpack must have been taken by mistake, because two students had the same one. Chances are that it is in the hall.

prompt.es: Responde a Leo: acepta su idea, dudes con una pista y propón lo más probable.

answer.text: That is possible, but it can't have been a teacher, because the teachers were in a meeting. The gate was open, so chances are that another student took it. I agree we should ask in the yard.
accepted: That is possible, but it can't have been a teacher, because the teachers were in a meeting. The gate was open, so chances are that another student took it. I agree we should ask in the yard.
I see what you mean, but a teacher can't have taken it, because the teachers were all in a meeting. Chances are that someone came in through the open gate. That is most likely.
Good point, Leo, but it can't have been a teacher, because they were in a meeting. The gate was open, so it may well have been another student.

feedback.es: La respuesta reconoce la idea, la cuestiona con una pista (la reunión) y propone una teoría más probable con chances are o may well.

origin.text: Leo dice: «I think a teacher might have taken Tom's bike.» Pistas: los profesores estaban en una reunión (meeting); el portón (gate) estaba abierto. Escribe entre 25 y 50 palabras.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué piensa quien habla sobre Leo.

choices.text: Leo was not in the office.

feedback.es: «Can't have been looking» descarta que Leo estuviera en la oficina: estaba en clase.

origin.audio: Leo can't have been looking for the keys in the office, because he was in class.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace Sara con la idea de Tom?

choices.text: She questions it politely with a reason.
She rejects it without a reason.

feedback.es: Sara dice «That is possible, but…» y da una razón: cuestiona la idea con amabilidad.

origin.text: Tom: «Chances are that the bag is in the office.» Sara: «That is possible, but the office was closed at lunch.»

prompt.es: Escribe una frase para aceptar la idea de Mia y proponer buscar en la cantina.

answer.text: I agree with you, let's look in the canteen first.
accepted: I agree with you, let's look in the canteen first.
I agree. Let's look in the canteen first.
I agree with you. Let's look there first.

feedback.es: Se acepta con I agree (sin am) y se propone la acción con let's + verbo base.

origin.text: Mia dice que la mochila está en la cantina. Tú estás de acuerdo y propones mirar allí primero.
